correctness.rationale: For every b≥2,t≥1, folding N modulo b^t-1 decreases N and weakly decreases digit sum until the unique positive representative M<b^t is reached. The residue class forces multiples of b-1. Explicit witnesses W_r=(b^t-1)(b^t+b^r+1) have digit sum (t+r)(b-1), and separated copies of M realize all larger admissible sums. For N<b^(2t), the two-block reduction A+B∈{M,2M} proves that only t(b-1) or 2t(b-1) can occur, while W_r achieves each intermediate weight in exactly 2t+1 digits. Arithmetic and boundary cases were directly reconstructed; `verify.py` tests 1728 constructions, 25200 lower-bound samples and 16 exhaustive small two-block cases. Experiments are not used as proof.

evidence: Phunphayap–Noppakaew–Pongsriiam, Theorems 2.1 and 2.4, give the divisibility restriction and all multiples of the original digit sum. For M=b^t-1, this covers only t(b-1),2t(b-1),3t(b-1), ... rather than intermediate (t+r)(b-1).
Toumi 2025, Theorem 1.2, concerns averaged distribution in modular residue classes under (digit-modulus,q-1)=1, not exact finite integer sum support under a fixed divisibility requirement.
Dartyge–Luca–Stănică 2009, Theorem 1, is about at least one nontrivial multiple preserving the original digit sum, rather than all prescribed higher sums.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An asymptotic distribution of digit-sum residue classes cannot establish the exact minimum, all admissible individual integer weights, and minimal finite base-b length. The broad 2023 directed-arc framework explicitly leaves exact outgoing sets open in general, and neither its stated inclusion nor its construction entails the new intermediate witnesses or short-length rigidity.

originality.rationale: A universal exact support formula and sharp intermediate shortest-length rigidity were not entailed by the closest published results. The 2016 binary lower bound and 2023 arc-set congruence and concatenation theorems are expressly credited; these do not prove the missing intermediate weights, which are constructed here. Primary 2025 arithmetic-progression paper studies asymptotic residue distribution and first-hitting issues (Remark 1.1), but not the exact intermediate first-hitting lengths or support in this family; targeted published-finding corpus and historical-claim comparisons returned no covering counterpart. Residual independent priority uncertainty is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Equivalent exact spectra might be folklore, a competition exercise, or formulated in digital-sum literature under different terminology.
Priority comparisons were limited to accessible primary papers, searchable literature and previous accessible claims, not an exhaustive universal search.
The direct arc-set predecessor was first public in March 2023; its later 2025 journal publication has not been treated as the first public date.

value.rationale: The complete all-base, all-exponent digital-weight spectrum of the natural moduli b^t-1 is a motivated exact arithmetic invariant, and its first intermediate weights have a sharp attained least digit length 2t+1. This resolves a natural special family of exact support questions left undetermined by congruence restrictions, and supplies more than a cheap normalization or numerical list. It does not give general modulus spectra or optimal lengths beyond the first gap.
